children: , the content delivery and cybersecurity company, rose 21.83% in premarket after it signed an $11.6 billion, seven-year contract to supply Anthropic with computing power. The deal, the largest in Akamai's history, gives the Claude developer access to central processing units and builds on a $1.8 billion agreement the two struck earlier this year.

Akamai expects capital spending tied to the contract to total about $5.5 billion, more than six times its entire 2025 capex, with most of it going on servers, chips and networking gear next year. CEO Tom Leighton said revenue from the Anthropic business should reach $150 million to $300 million next year and an annual run rate of about $1.7 billion by 2028.

Akamai also issued Anthropic a warrant to buy Series B shares at $111.33 each, convertible into 7.7 million common shares. A portion equal to about 2% of Akamai's common stock vests when the computing agreement starts in the second half of next year, with the rest vesting over the contract's term. Leighton called the warrant, Akamai's first in a cloud deal, "a serious step." It also lands as some investors question circular AI deals, in which suppliers and customers invest in each other.

title: Akamai Stock Rises 22% on $11.6 Billion Anthropic Deal
